title: Scheduled Auto-Renew Charges on Certificate Subscriptions
content:
**Renewals team service entry: scheduled auto-renew charges on SSL/TLS Certificates**

**1. When the charge falls due.** An auto-renew charge falls due on the product's auto-renew day before the subscription end date (30 days before the end date for every SSL/TLS Certificates product) of a subscription whose auto-renew is on and whose billing carries no renewal or auto-renew line for the term starting on that end date, and it is owed from that day.

**2. Scope.** Every support renewal is priced under the support renewal rule, and every renewal bought in the dashboard remains under the base renewal rule, which bills the tier's price for the years renewed plus the extra names for those years, reduced by the account tier's SSL certificate discount percentage and rounded half up to the cent; the volume ladder never applies to an auto-renew charge.

**3. One price, whatever pays it.** Every auto-renew charge that falls due is priced under the auto-renew charge rule, whatever pays it, and account credit pays it first, following the account charter: where the account credit balance on the day the charge falls due covers that amount in full, the account's credit run books it at that amount from account credit, and otherwise it is charged in full to the default card on file at that amount and booked under the auto-renew charge rule.

| Account credit balance on the day the charge falls due | Who books the charge | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| covers the auto-renew amount in full | the account's credit run, from account credit | the auto-renew amount priced under this rule |
| does not cover it in full | charged in full to the default card on file, booked under this rule | the same auto-renew amount |

**4. What the card charge books.** An auto-renew charge charged to the default card on file appears in the certificate billing history as an auto-renew line, paid by card, with a new Harborline order number, whose period starts on the previous subscription end date and ends on the new one; the subscription end date moves forward by the years renewed, counted from the previous end date.

**5. Situation of use and capability.** `charge_certificate_autorenewal_c41e0ea2` takes the scheduled auto-renew charge of one certificate subscription on the default payment card on file. One call bills one auto-renew line on the subscription for the years given, paid by card, with a newly issued Harborline order number, and moves the subscription end date that many calendar years later, counted from the current end date. The amount passed is billed exactly as given.

**6. How it is invoked.** The tool is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `charge_certificate_autorenewal_c41e0ea2` and then calls it.

**7. Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `certificate_id` | the reference number of the certificate subscription whose auto-renew charge is taken, as returned by the certificate subscription lookup | text id |
| `years` | the years the auto-renew adds to the subscription | 1 when it adds one year; 2 when it adds two years; 3 when it adds three years |
| `amount` | the auto-renew amount to bill | USD, 2 decimal places, signed, positive for this charge; any further decimals are rounded half up to the cent |

**8. Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the new auto-renew line's reference number (a text id), the order number (HL- followed by 8 digits), the amount billed in US dollars with two decimals, the covered period as two YYYY-MM-DD dates (the prior end date and the new end date) and the subscription's new end date (YYYY-MM-DD); the presence of the new end date means the charge was taken. The tool returns an error and books nothing when the amount is not a positive dollar figure ("the auto-renew amount must be a positive dollar figure"), when the years are not 1, 2 or 3 ("years must be 1, 2 or 3"), or when no certificate subscription has the reference given ("no certificate subscription" followed by that reference).

**Hypothetical illustration (invented values).** A call with a subscription reference, `years` 2 and `amount` 188.00 on a subscription ending 3 March 2033 returns a sentence reporting an auto-renew line billed 188.00 USD to the card on file for 2033-03-03 to 2035-03-03, and the subscription now ending on 2035-03-03.
